title: Snow and snowflakes
examples: Do all snowflakes look the same?
Can I see the shape of a snowflake?

explain.say: Snowflakes are tiny ice crystals that fall from clouds.
Most snowflakes have six sides, or six arms.
Every snowflake has its own pattern.
High in the cold clouds, water vapour freezes onto tiny specks of dust. This makes ice crystals.
In cold air, the crystals grow arms and become snowflakes.
Catch snowflakes on a dark glove on a cold day. Look closely at their shapes.

draw.text: See snowflakes on a cold day.

faq.q: Do all snowflakes have six sides?
faq.a: Yes, most do. Snowflakes grow six arms because of the way ice crystals form.
asks: What is the shape of a snowflake?

faq.q: Are all snowflakes exactly the same?
faq.a: Snowflakes can look alike, but up close each one has its own pattern.
High in cold clouds, water vapour freezes into tiny ice crystals. The crystals grow into snowflakes.
asks: What is the process of snow making?

faq.q: What is the best way to see a snowflake's sides?
faq.a: Catch one on a dark glove. Look closely with a magnifying glass.
asks: How do I check the sides?
What do I use to see snowflake details?

faq.q: Do snowflakes only form in the winter?
faq.a: Snow falls when the air is cold enough, usually in winter. Some very high mountains have snow all year.
asks: Does snow need to be very cold?

facts: Snowflakes are made of ice crystals.
Most snowflakes have a six-sided shape.
No two snowflakes are exactly alike.
Snowflakes form when water vapour freezes in cold air.

quiz.say: Count the arms of a snowflake. How many do most snowflakes have?

wrong.0: Four is too few, so count again.
wrong.2: Eight is too many, so count again.

quiz.say: Every snowflake is unique. What does unique mean?

options.show: it is one of a kind
options.say: it is one of a kind

quiz.why: Unique means there is only one like it.

wrong.1: The same is the opposite of unique.
wrong.2: Snowflakes are cold, but unique is about being one of a kind.

quiz.say: What do snowflakes need to form?
quiz.why: Water freezes into ice crystals in very cold air.

wrong.1: Wind can blow snow around, but cold air makes it.
